couplets.gloss: Kindly regard for other people is a rare loveliness, and the whole world only keeps running because of it.

edges.reason: Says the world stands only because this kindly regard is in it.
edges.quote: This world exists because of the surpassing beauty

couplets.gloss: Everything that makes living together pleasant depends on looking kindly on others; people who never do are dead weight on the world.

edges.reason: Rests the whole way of the world on this one grace.
edges.quote: The way of the world rests on kindly regard

edges.reason: The earth has to carry those without it as a load that gives her nothing.
edges.quote: a burden on the earth

couplets.gloss: A tune that doesn't fit the song is useless, and so is an eye that never looks kindly on anyone.

edges.reason: Sets an eye without kindly regard beside a melody that doesn’t fit the song: both have lost their point.
edges.quote: What use is an eye without kindly regard?

edges.reason: Asks what an eye is for, if not for looking on others with kindness.
edges.quote: an eye without kindly regard

couplets.gloss: If your eyes don't look on people with fitting kindness, what are they doing in your face?

edges.reason: Asks the use of eyes that fail to give others the regard they are due.
edges.quote: Eyes without kindly regard, in due measure

edges.reason: Reduces unkind eyes to features that only sit on the face and do no work.
edges.quote: only seem to be there in the face

couplets.gloss: Kindness is what makes an eye beautiful; without it, an eye is just an open wound.

edges.reason: Makes kindness the one thing that saves an eye from being a wound.
edges.quote: Kindly regard is the eye’s jewel

edges.reason: Names kindly regard as the jewel an eye wears.
edges.quote: the eye’s jewel

edges.reason: An eye empty of kindness is taken for a sore, not an organ of sight.
edges.quote: an eye is taken for a sore

couplets.gloss: People who have eyes but never look kindly on others are no more responsive than trees rooted in the ground.

edges.reason: Those whose eyes give others no regard are ranked no higher than vegetation.
edges.quote: whose eyes never turn kindly to others

edges.reason: Compares unfeeling people to trees standing fixed in the soil.
edges.quote: like trees fixed in the soil

couplets.gloss: Anyone without kindness in their eyes is really blind, and nobody who truly sees lacks that kindness.

edges.reason: Makes kindly regard the proof of real sight.
edges.quote: Those who have eyes are never without it

edges.reason: Turns blindness into the state of anyone without kindly regard.
edges.quote: Those without kindly regard have no eyes

couplets.gloss: The world belongs to those who can be kind to people without letting the job suffer for it.

edges.reason: Promises the earth only to kindness that leaves duty intact.
edges.quote: show kindly regard without ruining the work

couplets.gloss: The finest quality is to stay kind and patient even with those who have wronged you.
couplets.sensitive: counsels forbearance towards those who wrong you

edges.reason: Extends kindly regard even to people whose way is to hurt you.
edges.quote: Even with people whose way is to hurt you

edges.reason: Calls bearing with those who hurt you the highest quality.
edges.quote: show kindly regard and put up with it

couplets.gloss: People who aim at true graciousness will knowingly swallow poison a friend has poured, rather than shame them.
couplets.sensitive: praises knowingly accepting harm from another

edges.reason: Takes the courtesy everyone admires as far as drinking poison rather than refuse the one who poured it.
edges.quote: watch poison being poured, drink it

couplets.gloss: A ruler should treat spies and the science of statecraft as his two eyes.

edges.reason: Gives spies equal place with the renowned books as what a ruler sees by.
edges.quote: Spies and books of high repute

edges.reason: Speaks by name to the ruler about what he must take as his eyes.
edges.quote: a ruler should be clear

edges.reason: A ruler's sources of knowledge are pictured as the very organ of his sight.
edges.quote: these two are his eyes

couplets.gloss: A ruler's job is to find out quickly everything happening to everyone, every day.

edges.reason: Makes knowing at once what happens to everyone the ruler’s stated work.
edges.quote: a ruler’s work

edges.reason: Knowing all that happens to everyone, every day, is what a ruler’s spies are for.
edges.quote: To know quickly, every day, all that happens to everyone

couplets.gloss: A ruler who doesn't use agents to find out what's really happening has no chance of victory.

edges.reason: Rules out victory for the ruler who doesn’t spy through his spies.
edges.quote: doesn’t spy through his spies

edges.reason: Warns the ruler himself what he forfeits by staying uninformed.
edges.quote: A ruler who doesn’t spy

couplets.gloss: Agents must keep watch on everyone alike: government officials, the ruler's own relatives and his enemies.

edges.reason: Spares no one from scrutiny, not even the ruler's own family.
edges.quote: watches everyone alike

edges.reason: The work, the kin and the enemies are the ruler’s own, so this account of a spy is meant for him.
edges.quote: those who do your work, your own kin

edges.reason: Names those who do the ruler’s work first among those to be watched.
edges.quote: those who do your work

couplets.gloss: A good agent looks harmless, can't be stared down by anyone, and never lets a secret slip.

edges.reason: Lists what the agent needs: a harmless look, steady nerve, sealed lips.
edges.quote: A spy is someone with a look that draws no suspicion

edges.reason: Counts never letting a secret leak among a spy's essential gifts.
edges.quote: never lets anything spill

couplets.gloss: Agents should pose as monks and holy men, dig deep, and give nothing away whatever is done to them.

edges.reason: Has the spy go about in the form of those who have renounced.
edges.quote: the form of those who have renounced

edges.reason: Holds the secret fast even when the agent himself is made to suffer.
edges.quote: gives nothing away, whatever is done to them

couplets.gloss: A good agent can get hidden things out of people and reports what he learns plainly, leaving no doubt.

edges.reason: Picks out two skills: hearing what is hidden and being sure of what was learned.
edges.quote: can hear what has been hidden

couplets.gloss: Even what one agent brings back should be checked by sending another.

edges.reason: Refuses to take a single agent's word: one report must be tested by another.
edges.quote: have another spy find out too

couplets.gloss: Run your agents so that none knows the others, and believe a report only when three of them match.

edges.reason: Keeps agents unknown to one another and asks for three matching reports.
edges.quote: When three agree, believe it

edges.reason: Only the ruler running the service could be told to keep his spies apart.
edges.quote: Use spies so that one spy doesn’t know another

couplets.gloss: Don't honour your agents in public: doing so gives away your own secret.

edges.reason: Even a public reward would betray what the ruler needs kept hidden.
edges.quote: brought your own secret out into the open

edges.reason: The spy here is his own, so the one addressed is the ruler who employs him.
edges.quote: Don’t honour a spy

couplets.gloss: Only people with inner drive can be called rich; without it, do they truly own anything they have?

edges.reason: Lets drive alone earn the name of having, and doubts all other ownership.
edges.quote: Drive is what truly counts as having

edges.reason: Moves the title of possession from goods to a person’s own drive.
edges.quote: really have whatever else they have

couplets.gloss: Your spirit is what truly belongs to you, because money doesn't stay and will leave one day.

edges.reason: Prefers spirit to wealth because only spirit stays with a man.
edges.quote: To have spirit is to truly have something

edges.reason: Contrasts spirit as lasting property with riches that walk away.
edges.quote: Having wealth doesn’t last

couplets.gloss: People who have real drive don't sit wailing that they've lost everything.

edges.reason: Drive is the wealth in hand that keeps people from crying that all is lost.
edges.quote: hold lasting drive in their hand

couplets.gloss: Success asks the way to the door of someone whose drive never lets up.

edges.reason: Credits unwavering drive with drawing prosperity to itself.
edges.quote: whose drive never wavers

edges.reason: Fortune appears as a person stopping to ask directions to his house.
edges.quote: Good Fortune inquireth the way to his home

couplets.gloss: A water flower's stem rises as high as the water, and a person rises as high as their spirit.

edges.reason: Makes a person's spirit the exact gauge of how high they rise.
edges.quote: People rise as high as their spirit

edges.reason: The bloom grows with the water that feeds it, as a person grows with their spirit.
edges.quote: the measure of the luxuriance of its flower

edges.reason: The depth of the water sets how long a flower’s stem grows, as spirit sets how high people rise.
edges.quote: The stem of a water flower is as long as the water is deep

couplets.gloss: Always aim high: even if you fall short, the aim itself keeps its honour.

edges.reason: Urges every thought towards rising, for such an aim does not fail even when it fails.
edges.quote: Let all your thoughts be of rising higher

edges.reason: Tells one who fell short that a high aim has the nature of not failing.
edges.quote: Even when it fails, it has the nature of not failing

couplets.gloss: Strong-spirited people don't buckle when beaten; a wounded elephant just digs its feet in harder.

edges.reason: Says those with drive do not falter even when things fall apart.
edges.quote: The strong don’t falter when things fall apart

edges.reason: The struck elephant stands its ground instead of giving way.
edges.quote: An elephant struck by a mass of arrows stands its ground

edges.reason: The mass of arrows is the blow of ruin, and it doesn’t bring the strong down.
edges.quote: a mass of arrows

edges.reason: Offers someone whose plans have fallen apart a picture of standing firm under the wound.
edges.quote: don’t falter when things fall apart

couplets.gloss: People with no spirit will never know the pride of being openly and endlessly generous.

edges.reason: Shows what lack of spirit costs: the pride of being generous.
edges.quote: Those without spirit will never have the pride

couplets.gloss: Huge and sharp-tusked as it is, the elephant still panics when a tiger leaps at it.

edges.reason: Bulk and tusks fail the elephant: spirit, not size, decides the contest.
edges.quote: huge and sharp of tusk, yet it fears

edges.reason: The giant’s fear before the tiger shows size without spirit.
edges.quote: it fears a tiger’s attack

couplets.gloss: Inner drive is the only real strength; people without it are logs that happen to be in human form.
couplets.sensitive: calls people without drive lifeless wood

edges.reason: Declares high spirit to be the only strength worth the name.
edges.quote: A person’s strength is wealth of spirit

edges.reason: People without spirit are trees in human shape.
edges.quote: Those without it are trees

couplets.gloss: A family's light could burn forever, but laziness fouls the air around it until it goes out.

edges.reason: Laziness is the grime that puts out a family’s unfailing lamp.
edges.quote: the grime called laziness

edges.reason: Pictures the family as a lamp meant to stay lit.
edges.quote: The unfailing lamp called family

couplets.gloss: Anyone who wants their family to stand strong must treat laziness as the danger it is and keep clear of it.

edges.reason: Tells those who want a true family to treat laziness as what it is.
edges.quote: treat laziness as the laziness it is

edges.reason: Takes making a family truly a family as the goal worth shunning laziness for.
edges.quote: want their family to be a true family

couplets.gloss: The fool who cherishes laziness will see his family collapse before he himself dies.

edges.reason: Says the fool who carries laziness within sees the family die first, in the fool’s own lifetime.
edges.quote: carries laziness within

couplets.gloss: When people sink into laziness and attempt nothing worthwhile, their family falls apart and their faults multiply.

edges.reason: Two costs follow idleness here: the family is ruined and faults multiply.
edges.quote: the family dies and faults multiply

couplets.gloss: Delay, forgetfulness, laziness and oversleeping feel comfortable, and they are exactly what carries doomed people to their end.

edges.reason: Groups idleness with delay, forgetting and sleep as the habits of the doomed.
edges.quote: Delay, forgetfulness, laziness and sleep

edges.reason: These habits are a boat that people board gladly, and it carries them to ruin.
edges.quote: the boat that those bound for ruin desire

edges.reason: Names delay first among the four that carry people to ruin.
edges.quote: Delay, forgetfulness

couplets.gloss: Lazy people never really get ahead, even when they have powerful backers.

edges.reason: Even with all that the lords of the earth hold, the lazy can’t win any great good.
edges.quote: the lazy won’t easily win any great good

couplets.gloss: People who are lazy and try nothing worthwhile end up hearing constant scolding and contempt.

edges.reason: Scolding and scorn are what the idle have to sit and hear.
edges.quote: will hear words of rebuke and scorn

couplets.gloss: Once laziness settles into a family, that family soon ends up enslaved to its enemies.

edges.reason: Laziness settling in someone of good family ends in slavery to their enemies.
edges.quote: make them a slave to their enemies

couplets.gloss: Whatever has gone wrong in a family ends the moment its head stops being lazy.

edges.reason: Shows how much laziness was costing: end it and the faults in family and manhood go.
edges.quote: ends the rule of laziness over him

couplets.gloss: A ruler who is never lazy can win all the lands that Vishnu paced out in three strides, which means everything.

edges.reason: Freedom from laziness alone would win a ruler all that was crossed by the one who measured with his feet.
edges.quote: everything the one who measured with his feet strode over

edges.reason: Holds out this vast promise to a ruler in particular.
edges.quote: A ruler free of laziness

couplets.gloss: Never back away from a task because it looks too hard: effort itself gives you what you need to do it.

edges.reason: Effort itself supplies the greatness that a daunted person thinks is missing.
edges.quote: Effort will give you greatness

edges.reason: Speaks straight to someone about to say a task is impossible.
edges.quote: Don’t lose heart and say

couplets.gloss: Be careful not to leave a job half done: the world drops people who don't finish what they start.

edges.reason: Demands that work once begun be carried through to its end.
edges.quote: take care not to let the work fail

edges.reason: Warns anyone tempted to drop a task midway that the world writes off quitters.
edges.quote: The world leaves those who leave work undone

couplets.gloss: The pride of being able to help everyone belongs only to people who never shirk hard effort.

edges.reason: Only one with the quality of effort can know the pride of helping others.
edges.quote: the fine quality called effort

couplets.gloss: Generosity from someone who won't work soon fails, as useless as a sword held by one who can't fight.

edges.reason: An idle man's giving cannot last, any more than a blade in hands unfit for it.
edges.quote: someone without effort

edges.reason: The sword here is a weapon held by one who will never use it.
edges.quote: a sword in a eunuch’s hand

couplets.sensitive: uses a eunuch as the image of what is useless

couplets.gloss: Someone who prefers work to pleasure becomes the support their friends and family lean on, and dries their tears.

edges.reason: Choosing work over pleasure makes a man the pillar his people lean on.
edges.quote: wants work, not pleasure

couplets.gloss: Hard work creates wealth, and not trying lets poverty move in.

edges.reason: Effort is what builds prosperity.
edges.quote: Effort builds prosperity

edges.reason: Lack of effort brings in one thing only, and that is want.
edges.quote: Lack of effort lets want in

couplets.gloss: Misfortune lives in laziness, while the goddess of wealth lives in the efforts of those who aren't lazy.

edges.reason: Makes laziness the house where dark Misfortune lives.
edges.quote: dark Misfortune lives in laziness

edges.reason: Places the lady of the lotus inside the effort of those without laziness.
edges.quote: she of the lotus in the effort

edges.reason: She of the lotus and dark Misfortune each choose a dwelling by a person’s habits.
edges.quote: she of the lotus

couplets.gloss: Bad luck is no disgrace, but knowingly refusing to make an effort is.

edges.reason: Puts the disgrace on refusing to work, not on the outcome.
edges.quote: know what must be known and make no effort

edges.reason: Clears whoever tried and lost: lacking a favouring fate is no disgrace.
edges.quote: The lack of a favouring fate disgraces no one

couplets.gloss: Even if the gods won't grant what you're after, effort still pays you for the sweat you put in.

edges.reason: Promises effort its wages even when god won’t grant the result.
edges.quote: effort pays the wages of your body’s toil

edges.reason: Answers the sense that god is against you: the effort is still paid.
edges.quote: Even if god won’t allow it

couplets.gloss: People who keep working without let-up or giving in will see even fate turn its back and retreat.

edges.reason: Striving without faltering is what lets a person see the back of fate.
edges.quote: strive without faltering

edges.reason: Tells one who feels doomed that refusing to give in can beat fate itself.
edges.quote: see the back of fate itself

couplets.gloss: When trouble comes, smile at it: nothing helps you push through hardship as much.

edges.reason: Makes laughter the strongest stand one can take against trouble.
edges.quote: Laugh when trouble comes

edges.reason: Gives someone beset by trouble a plain first move: meet it laughing.
edges.quote: Laugh when trouble comes

couplets.gloss: Even a flood of trouble shrinks away once a clever mind stops and thinks calmly about it.

edges.reason: A wise mind, once set to it, makes even a flood of trouble die away.
edges.quote: sets their mind to it

edges.reason: Trouble is measured as a whole sea, and still it gives way.
edges.quote: A whole sea of troubles

edges.reason: Promises the swamped that collecting the mind is enough to bring the flood down.
edges.quote: Even a flood of trouble dies away

couplets.gloss: Those who don't let trouble upset them are the ones who give trouble itself a hard time.
keywords: not letting things get to you

edges.reason: Turns the tables: refusing to be troubled leaves trouble itself the loser.
edges.quote: will give trouble trouble

couplets.gloss: Someone who pushes through every obstacle like an ox hauling a load leaves those obstacles defeated.

edges.reason: Pulling through every blocked place like an ox leaves the trouble itself in trouble.
edges.quote: like an ox, pulls through every blocked place

couplets.gloss: When someone doesn't crumble however many troubles pile up, it's the troubles that are in trouble.

edges.reason: One who stays unbroken as troubles pile up leaves the troubles themselves in trouble.
edges.quote: the troubles that reach an unbroken person

edges.reason: Fits trouble piling on trouble: stay unbroken and it is the troubles that suffer.
edges.quote: Even if they come heaped one on another

couplets.gloss: People who don't gloat when they gain something won't wail when they lose it.

edges.reason: Whoever never clung to gain has no reason to cry out at loss.
edges.quote: never clung to what they gained

couplets.gloss: The wise accept that the body is there to be hit by trouble, so disaster doesn't shake them.

edges.reason: Expecting the body to be struck, the wise stay unshaken when the blow lands.
edges.quote: the body is a target for suffering

couplets.gloss: Someone who doesn't chase pleasure and accepts that hardship is natural doesn't really suffer when setbacks come.

edges.reason: Taking suffering as natural removes its power to bring sorrow.
edges.quote: says suffering is natural

couplets.gloss: If you don't revel in pleasure when things go well, you won't be crushed by pain when they go badly.

edges.reason: Ties pain in bad days to pleasure chased in good ones, so restraint spares both.
edges.quote: won’t feel sorrow in times of sorrow

couplets.gloss: Treat hardship as a joy and you will earn a standing that even your enemies admire.

edges.reason: Taking strain as joy wins the praise of one's own enemies.
edges.quote: take what hurts as joy

couplets.sensitive: counsel to take pain as joy could reach someone enduring mistreatment

couplets.gloss: A good minister is one who knows the means, the timing and the way to carry out difficult undertakings.

edges.reason: Sets the test for a minister: excellence in means, time, method and the work itself.
edges.quote: A minister is someone who excels

couplets.gloss: A minister needs firmness, care for the people, learning and hard work, on top of the skills already named.

edges.reason: Counts off the marks that make up a minister’s five qualities.
edges.quote: a minister excels in all five

edges.reason: Learning is named among the minister’s marks.
edges.quote: learning and knowing

edges.reason: Firmness in the work opens the list of his marks.
edges.quote: Firmness

edges.reason: Hard personal labour is required of him too, not only thought.
edges.quote: effort

couplets.gloss: A capable minister can split enemy alliances, keep friends close and win back those who have turned hostile.

edges.reason: Measures an able minister by three skills: to part allies, keep friends, reunite foes.
edges.quote: A minister is someone who can split others apart

couplets.gloss: A minister must be good at choosing what to do, at working out how to do it, and at giving clear, decisive advice.

edges.reason: Requires a firm, unhedged opinion from the one who advises.
edges.quote: speak with certainty

edges.reason: Asks for care in choosing projects and how to carry them out.
edges.quote: see clearly, act after weighing

couplets.gloss: The best counsellor knows what is right, is well taught and measured in speech, and always sees how to handle things.

edges.reason: Describes the one to have beside you in counsel: righteous, full in speech, knowing how to act.
edges.quote: a companion in counsel

couplets.gloss: What's too subtle for people who combine a sharp natural mind with book learning?

edges.reason: Sharp wit is one half of the pair that nothing can stand before.
edges.quote: sharp wit

edges.reason: Book learning added to wit leaves no subtlety able to stand against it.
edges.quote: book learning too

couplets.gloss: Even when you know the theory, act in line with how the world really works.

edges.reason: Tells those who know the method to know also how the world is.
edges.quote: know the nature of the world

couplets.gloss: Even if the ruler is a fool who blocks all advice, the person beside him must still tell him what is right.

edges.reason: Keeps the adviser speaking even when each word is thwarted.
edges.quote: tell him what is good for him

edges.reason: States the duty of the one at the ruler’s side.
edges.quote: the duty of the one at his side

couplets.gloss: A minister who secretly plots against his ruler does more damage than hundreds of millions of enemies.

edges.reason: Rates one plotter at your side as worse than a vast enemy host.
edges.quote: one minister at your side who plots harm

edges.reason: Turns on a minister who plots against the ruler he sits beside.
edges.quote: one minister at your side

couplets.gloss: People who can't follow through may plan perfectly and still never finish anything.

edges.reason: Even well-ordered plans stay unfinished for those without the skill and firmness to carry them out.
edges.quote: will leave them unfinished

couplets.gloss: Being good with words is a gift in a class of its own, separate from every other blessing.

edges.reason: Ranks a good tongue as a good apart from every other.
edges.quote: a good not found among any other goods

couplets.gloss: Both success and ruin come from what you say, so guard carefully against careless words.

edges.reason: Places the power of life and death in the tongue.
edges.quote: Death and life are in the power of the tongue

edges.reason: Because so much hangs on it, demands a guard against any slip of speech.
edges.quote: guard carefully against any slip in your speech

couplets.gloss: Real eloquence holds those who are listening and makes even those who aren't want to hear more.

edges.reason: Sets the test of true speech: it binds those who hear and draws even those who haven’t.
edges.quote: Speech is that which holds its hearers fast

couplets.gloss: Size up the situation, then say what suits it: nothing does more for doing right and doing well.

edges.reason: Says nothing is worth more than weighing the circumstances first, then speaking to fit.
edges.quote: Know the right way and speak your words

couplets.gloss: Say something only when you know no one can answer it with anything better.

edges.reason: Asks for words so sound that no other words can answer them.
edges.quote: no other word can beat it

couplets.gloss: The mark of the finest people is to speak so others love to listen, and to grasp what's useful in what others say.

edges.reason: Joins making others want to hear with taking the use of what they say, as the way of the flawless.
edges.quote: speak so that others want to hear

couplets.gloss: Nobody can beat a person in argument who speaks well, doesn't slip up and isn't afraid.

edges.reason: Fluent speech backed by calm nerve cannot be beaten in debate.
edges.quote: hard for anyone to beat

couplets.gloss: The world moves quickly to do what is asked by those who can speak in a clear, orderly and pleasing way.

edges.reason: Orderly, persuasive speech puts the whole world at the speaker's call.
edges.quote: The world quickly does as it is asked

couplets.gloss: People who can't say what they mean in a few clean words end up in love with talking at length.

edges.reason: Holds up a few flawless words as the mark the long-winded miss.
edges.quote: a few flawless words

edges.reason: Treats a love of much talk as what is left to those who cannot be brief.
edges.quote: surely desire to say many

couplets.gloss: People who can't explain what they have learned are like a flower in bloom with no scent.

edges.reason: Learning that cannot be put into words for others is learning wasted.
edges.quote: can’t unfold what they have learned

edges.reason: A bloom without fragrance shows learning that never reaches anyone.
edges.quote: flowers that bloom in clusters but have no scent

couplets.gloss: Good allies bring success, but doing things the right way brings you everything you could want.

edges.reason: Ranks clean action above allies: they bring success, it brings every desire.
edges.quote: Good deeds bring all you want

couplets.gloss: Always stay away from actions that don't bring both a good name and real benefit.

edges.reason: Bars any work that doesn’t bring good along with fame.
edges.quote: keep away from work that doesn’t bring good along with fame

couplets.gloss: If you want to go up in the world, give up anything you do that would dim your good name.

edges.reason: Anyone wanting to rise must refuse whatever would dim their light.
edges.quote: must stop doing what dims their light

couplets.gloss: Clear-sighted people won't do anything shameful even when they have fallen on hard times.

edges.reason: Even trouble does not excuse a shameful act.
edges.quote: won’t do anything shameful

couplets.gloss: Don't do what will make you cry out in regret; and if you've done it, at least don't do it again.

edges.reason: Tests an act by whether it will wring a cry of regret from the doer.
edges.quote: cry “What have I done?”

edges.reason: Gives one already ashamed a plain course: do not do it again.
edges.quote: it is good not to do the like again

couplets.gloss: Never do what good people condemn, even to save your own mother from starving.

edges.reason: Holds the line even where a starving mother would seem to excuse crossing it.
edges.quote: don’t do what the worthy condemn

couplets.gloss: The deep poverty of good people is far better than riches gained by shameful means.

edges.reason: Puts honest want far above wealth got by disgrace.
edges.quote: the deep poverty of the worthy

edges.reason: Speaks to anyone weighing easy money: better to stay poor and clean.
edges.quote: prosperity gained by wearing disgrace

couplets.gloss: People who won't avoid what morality forbids will suffer for it, even if their schemes work.

edges.reason: Grief follows forbidden means even when the scheme succeeds.
edges.quote: brings pain even if it succeeds

couplets.gloss: What you take from people while they weep will leave you while you weep; honest gains, even if lost for a while, bear fruit later.

edges.reason: What is good, even when lost for a time, bears fruit afterwards.
edges.quote: What is good, even if lost, bears fruit afterwards

couplets.gloss: Building wealth through deceit is like storing water in a pot of unfired clay: it will all seep away.

edges.reason: Crooked means can no more keep wealth than raw clay can keep water.
edges.quote: pouring water into a pot of raw clay

edges.reason: Treats riches heaped up by trickery as bound to drain away.
edges.quote: wealth made by deceit

edges.reason: Shows one tempted by a shady gain that such money will not stay.
edges.quote: wealth made by deceit

couplets.gloss: Being strong in action really comes down to being strong in mind; nothing else counts.

edges.reason: Says firmness in action is nothing but firmness of mind.
edges.quote: Firmness in action is a person’s firmness of mind

couplets.gloss: Thinkers agree on two rules: steer clear of what will fail, and don't lose heart when setbacks come.

edges.reason: Half the rule of those who have looked into it is not to give way once harm comes.
edges.quote: not giving way once it comes

couplets.gloss: Real strength lies in revealing a plan only once it's done; showing it halfway brings trouble you can't undo.

edges.reason: Holds back a purpose until it is achieved, since early disclosure breeds obstacles.
edges.quote: so that it shows only at the end

couplets.gloss: Anyone can say what they'll do; actually doing it the way they said is the hard part.

edges.reason: Talk is easy for all: doing the thing as it was undertaken is rare.
edges.quote: Doing it as you said is hard

couplets.gloss: The firmness of people who've proved themselves reaches the top and earns them respect from the leader and everyone else.

edges.reason: The firmness of the excellent reaches the ruler and earns lasting regard.
edges.quote: firmness in action of those who have risen to excellence

couplets.gloss: If people are firm enough of will, they will get what they set out to get, just the way they meant to.

edges.reason: Firmness gets what was planned, in the way it was planned.
edges.quote: if they are firm

couplets.gloss: Don't look down on someone for how they look: some are as small and vital as the pin that holds a great cart's wheel.

edges.reason: Warns against sizing a person up by looks, since the plainest may hold everything together.
edges.quote: Don’t scorn people for how they look

edges.reason: The small axle pin carries the great chariot, as an unimpressive person may.
edges.quote: the axle pin of the great rolling chariot

couplets.gloss: Once you've clearly decided on something, stop hesitating and carry it out with energy.

edges.reason: Once the choice is clearly made, forbids wavering and delay.
edges.quote: don’t waver or delay

couplets.gloss: Stick firmly with work that brings lasting good, even if it causes you great pain along the way.

edges.reason: Asks for resolve in work that brings joy, whatever pain comes.
edges.quote: be resolute and do the work that brings joy

edges.reason: Speaks to one worn down by a worthwhile task: press on to the end.
edges.quote: Even if great pain comes

couplets.gloss: However strong people are in other ways, the world has no use for those who don't want to do great things.

edges.reason: Without the wish to do great deeds, other virtues win no one's notice.
edges.quote: have not the ambition to do great deeds

edges.reason: The Tamil's point is firmness in action, without which all other firmness is ignored.
edges.quote: the world doesn’t want those who don’t want firmness in action

couplets.gloss: The purpose of thinking things over is to reach a decision, and once you've reached it, delaying is a mistake.

edges.reason: States what weighing a matter is for: arriving at a decision.
edges.quote: The end of deliberation is to reach a decision

edges.reason: Once a decision stands, holding back its execution is called wrong.
edges.quote: sit in delay is wrong

couplets.gloss: Take your time over what can wait, but don't delay a moment over what has to be done now.

edges.reason: Sorts work into the leisurely and the urgent, each with its own pace.
edges.quote: Take your time over what should be done slowly

edges.reason: Tells someone who keeps delaying that some work must be done without delay.
edges.quote: Don’t delay over what must be done without delay

couplets.gloss: Go directly for your goal whenever you can; when you can't, take whatever route is still open.

edges.reason: Allows direct action where it can be done, and whatever way will work where it can’t.
edges.quote: look for the way that will work

couplets.gloss: Unfinished work and half-beaten enemies are like sparks left burning: they grow back and destroy the careless.

edges.reason: Warns that work left undone flares up later against the careless.
edges.quote: what is left of a task or an enemy

edges.reason: Unfinished business is a spark that seems dead but grows to overwhelm.
edges.quote: what is left of a fire

couplets.gloss: Before acting, think clearly through five things: your means, your tools, the task itself, the timing and the place.

edges.reason: Gives a five-point review to clear before any action is taken.
edges.quote: weigh all five until the darkness clears

edges.reason: Wealth comes first on the list of five.
edges.quote: Wealth

edges.reason: Time is the third thing to weigh.
edges.quote: time

edges.reason: The right ground closes the list.
edges.quote: the place

couplets.gloss: Before you act, look at what it will take to finish, what could block you, and what you stand to gain.

edges.reason: Sets out what to reckon first: the finish, the obstacles and the gain.
edges.quote: Look at the finish, the obstacles, and the gain

edges.reason: Gives anyone weighing a venture three things to settle before committing.
edges.quote: Look at the finish, the obstacles, and the gain you will reach

couplets.gloss: To do a job well, find out how it's really done from someone who knows it inside out.

edges.reason: Makes learning the mind of one who knows the task from inside the way to do it.
edges.quote: someone who knows that task from the inside

couplets.gloss: Use one project to get another done, the way hunters use a tame elephant to catch a wild one.

edges.reason: Shows how to make one undertaking carry a second.
edges.quote: To get one task done by means of another

edges.reason: One wet-cheeked elephant used to bind another models work that wins more work.
edges.quote: bind a wet-cheeked elephant with another elephant

couplets.gloss: Be even quicker to win over your opponents than you are to do good to your friends.

edges.reason: Ranks winning over those not with you as more urgent even than doing good to a friend.
edges.quote: win over those not with you

couplets.gloss: Weak parties shouldn't live in fear: when the chance comes they should make terms with the strong.

edges.reason: Urges those who hold little to own their weakness and bow to the great for terms.
edges.quote: will bow to the great

couplets.sensitive: Tells the weak to submit to the strong.

couplets.gloss: An ambassador needs a loving heart, a good family background and the manners that win over rulers.

edges.reason: Names the marks that fit a man for an embassy.
edges.quote: the qualities of an envoy

edges.reason: Loving-kindness comes first in the envoy’s list.
edges.quote: Loving-kindness

edges.reason: A good family is required of him too.
edges.quote: birth in a good family

edges.reason: The qualities rulers desire complete the three.
edges.quote: the qualities rulers desire

couplets.gloss: Love, wisdom and carefully weighed speech are the three things a diplomat can't do without.

edges.reason: Calls these three indispensable to whoever carries a message abroad.
edges.quote: can’t do without these three

edges.reason: Loving-kindness leads the envoy’s three needs.
edges.quote: Loving-kindness

edges.reason: Sound judgment is the second.
edges.quote: understanding

edges.reason: The third is command of words.
edges.quote: skill in well-weighed speech

couplets.gloss: Whoever speaks for his side before foreign rulers must be the most learned among the learned.

edges.reason: One who speaks for victory among men of the spear is the envoy in all but name.
edges.quote: speaks for victory among men of the spear

edges.reason: Requires deep learning of the one speaking for his master.
edges.quote: a master of the books among those who know the books

couplets.gloss: Send as your representative someone who combines good sense, an impressive presence and thorough learning.

edges.reason: Says who should be the one to go on embassies.
edges.quote: Let the one who has all three

edges.reason: Intelligence heads the three things that qualify him.
edges.quote: understanding

edges.reason: Learning completes the three, after understanding and presence.
edges.quote: well-tested learning

couplets.gloss: An ambassador does good for his side by being brief, avoiding unpleasant words and speaking so as to please.

edges.reason: Lays down how an envoy’s manner of speaking brings about good.
edges.quote: An envoy sums up

edges.reason: Brevity, the few well-chosen words of real eloquence, comes first.
edges.quote: sums up

edges.reason: Speaking so that people smile is the third means.
edges.quote: speaks so that people smile

edges.reason: Dropping what is harsh is the second means.
edges.quote: drops what is harsh

couplets.gloss: A diplomat is one who has studied, isn't cowed by hostile eyes, speaks convincingly and knows what suits the moment.

edges.reason: Collects what an envoy must bring to a foreign court.
edges.quote: An envoy is learned

edges.reason: Study is the first of the four.
edges.quote: learned

edges.reason: Not fearing a hard stare is the courage asked of him before a hostile ruler.
edges.quote: unafraid of a hard stare

edges.reason: Speech that carries conviction is third.
edges.quote: speaks so that it goes home

edges.reason: A feel for what each moment calls for completes the list.
edges.quote: knows what suits the time

couplets.gloss: The best envoy knows his duty, considers timing and place, and thinks before he speaks.

edges.reason: Says who is the fittest man to send.
edges.quote: The finest is the one

edges.reason: Suits words to time and place, weighing them before they are spoken.
edges.quote: watches the time, knows the place

couplets.gloss: An envoy needs purity, firm nerve and the backing of allies, and with these he delivers his message faithfully.

edges.reason: Sets the marks for the one who carries a message.
edges.quote: one who carries a message

edges.reason: Resolve is the third of the marks.
edges.quote: resolve

edges.reason: Purity opens the list of marks.
edges.quote: Purity

couplets.gloss: The person to carry a ruler's message abroad is someone firm who will never utter a word that shames his side.

edges.reason: Fixes on who is fit to carry a message to rulers.
edges.quote: The one who delivers a message to rulers

edges.reason: He keeps every scarring word from leaving his mouth.
edges.quote: lets no scarring word slip

couplets.gloss: Even when it could cost him his life, a true ambassador delivers for his master and does not shrink back.

edges.reason: Holds up the true envoy at the moment of greatest danger.
edges.quote: even if it brings his death

edges.reason: Serves his master's interest even under threat of death.
edges.quote: brings about what is good for his ruler

couplets.gloss: Those who deal with powerful rulers should be like people warming themselves at a fire: not too close, not too far.

edges.reason: Instructs whoever would live near rulers.
edges.quote: Those who live close to quarrelsome rulers

edges.reason: A fire warms at the right distance and burns when too near, and so does a ruler.
edges.quote: warming themselves at a fire

edges.reason: Gives anyone reliant on a mighty superior a working rule of distance.
edges.quote: neither too far nor too near

couplets.gloss: Not wanting the things the ruler himself wants is the way to gain lasting benefit from him.

edges.reason: Reveals what brings lasting prosperity from rulers.
edges.quote: lasting prosperity from those rulers

edges.reason: For anyone dependent on a superior: don't reach for what they want for themselves.
edges.quote: Not wanting what rulers want

couplets.gloss: Be careful above all about the serious mistakes: once someone suspects you, nobody can clear your name.
In the presence of important people, don't whisper in someone's ear or share a private smile.

edges.reason: Rules of bearing for someone standing near those in power.
edges.quote: In the presence of the truly great

edges.reason: Whispers and shared laughter near the great are slights to be avoided.
edges.quote: put a stop to whispers in the ear and shared laughter

couplets.gloss: Don't eavesdrop or pry into what's being kept from you; wait until you're told the secret.
Read the ruler's mood and the moment, then say what he wants to hear and won't object to.

edges.reason: Teaches one who must speak before a ruler how to choose his moment.
edges.quote: Read the signs, consider the time

edges.reason: Weighing the hearer's mood and the occasion comes before any word.
edges.quote: Read the signs, consider the time

edges.reason: Transfers directly to a moody boss: read the mood and the time, then speak.
edges.quote: say what is needed and not disliked

couplets.gloss: Tell the ruler what he'll be glad to hear, and never say what's pointless, even if he asks.
keywords: what not to say to your boss

edges.reason: Governs what may and may not be said before a ruler.
edges.quote: Say what is wanted

edges.reason: Even being asked is no reason to say what serves no purpose.
edges.quote: What is of no use, never say, even if asked

couplets.gloss: Don't take a ruler lightly because he's young or related to you: treat the position he holds with respect.

edges.reason: Warns those close to a ruler by age or kinship against familiarity.
edges.quote: Don’t scorn someone as young or as your kin

edges.reason: Demands conduct fit for the light in a ruler, whatever his age or relation.
edges.quote: the light that stands in them

couplets.gloss: Clear-sighted people don't do what displeases the ruler just because they think they're in favour.

edges.reason: Shows how the clear-sighted carry themselves when a ruler has taken them up.
edges.quote: We have been accepted

edges.reason: Favour is no licence: the wise still take care not to displease a ruler.
edges.quote: do what isn’t acceptable

edges.reason: Warns anyone enjoying a superior's favour not to presume on it.
edges.quote: think “We have been accepted”

couplets.gloss: Doing improper things because you've known the ruler a long time leads to your ruin.

edges.reason: Foretells the end of those who lean on closeness to a ruler.
edges.quote: The intimacy that says “We go back a long way”

edges.reason: Long acquaintance gives no licence to slight a ruler: those who presume on it perish.
edges.quote: does what isn’t fitting brings ruin

ideaLinks.reason: Without spirit behind it, the pride of being generous can’t be had.
ideaLinks.quote: Those without spirit will never have the pride of thinking

ideaLinks.reason: Laziness puts out the family’s lamp, brings it down and leaves it in ruin.
ideaLinks.quote: The unfailing lamp called family goes out

ideaLinks.reason: The pride of helping others rests in effort and nowhere else.
ideaLinks.quote: The pride called helping others rests in the fine quality called effort

ideaLinks.reason: An idle man's generosity cannot last: giving depends on the labour behind it.
ideaLinks.quote: Helping others, in someone without effort, will come to nothing
Lack of effort lets want in

ideaLinks.reason: Effort and its lack are set side by side, one building prosperity and the other letting want in.
ideaLinks.quote: Effort builds prosperity. Lack of effort lets want in.

ideaLinks.reason: Striving without faltering lets a person see the back of fate.
ideaLinks.quote: will see the back of fate itself

ideaLinks.reason: One who doesn’t crave joy in times of joy is spared sorrow in times of sorrow.
ideaLinks.quote: Someone who doesn’t crave joy in times of joy won’t feel sorrow in times of sorrow.

ideaLinks.reason: Perfect plans go unfinished when the will wavers in the doing.
ideaLinks.quote: The irresolute may even plan perfectly: but they will waver in the course of the execution and will never accomplish their designs

ideaLinks.reason: Thinking a matter through is meant to end in a firm decision.
ideaLinks.quote: The end of deliberation is to reach a decision
